findings.description: SYS-CFG-001 takes task periods from the configuration block. SYS-SUP-001 and SYS-SUP-005 depend on the configured release schedule, but the release rules in SYS-CFG-003 and SYS-CFG-009 cover the defaults only. The set leaves it unclear whether the timer-driven scheduler in CON-SUP-006 uses a changed period or whether only supervision uses it under STK-SUP-004.
findings.requested_change: Define which configured periods govern application releases and which govern supervision. Record any owner decision needed on the supported periods and use one defined release schedule for the alive and flow checks.

findings.description: A block can fail the CRC check under CON-SUP-107 and contain an out-of-range value under CON-SUP-115. SYS-RST-012 requires a software reset for the first fault and SYS-RST-003 requires a latch for the second. OP-SYS-040 leaves the validity and precedence of these checks open.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved check order and define the resulting report, history entry, reset and latch behavior when integrity and range checks can both fail.

findings.description: After a retained CON-SUP-110 latch and a successful startup, SYS-SAFE-010 and SYS-SAFE-011 hold the external signals low. SYS-MEM-004, SYS-SUP-001 and SYS-MEM-005 through SYS-MEM-008 lack a common rule for the application and supervision functions active in that state.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved latched-state policy consistently to task releases, supervision, integrity checking, watchdog service, diagnostic service and fault handling.

findings.description: SYS-RST-004 now assigns the reset the code of the fault that starts the SYS-RST-001 deadline or triggers SYS-RST-012. Its rationale identifies this as an unapproved interpretation of CON-SUP-110. When two different faults precede one reset, that choice changes the next startup's latch count.
findings.requested_change: Use the approved fault-code attribution rule across reset timing, report ordering and latch counting. Update the mixed-code verification cases to exercise that rule.

findings.description: Startup messages, fault reports and service replies share the CON-SUP-007 line. An eight-report GET FAULTS response can occupy it longer than the CON-SUP-112 fault-report budget. Receipt of a fault during such a response has no agreed frame-handling or deadline precedence rule.
findings.requested_change: Define admitted simultaneous traffic, maximum frame lengths and the ordering or interruption of transmissions. Check that the resulting rules meet the approved report and service deadlines.

findings.description: The configuration producer and SYS-MEM-002 checker can use identical CRC parameters and still disagree about the bytes covered under CON-SUP-107. OP-SYS-005 leaves serialization, the covered range and treatment of the stored CRC field open.
findings.requested_change: Reference an approved producer-to-checker block format and include reference blocks with independently calculated expected CRC values.

findings.description: SYS-SAFE-007 and SYS-SAFE-008 cite SYS-SAFE-003 for the latched holds under CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-115, which SYS-SAFE-010 and SYS-SAFE-011 own. SYS-RST-012 cites SYS-RST-002 for report-before-reset ordering, which SYS-RST-013 owns. SYS-RST-013 cites SYS-WDG-005 for window-watchdog cessation, which SYS-WDG-007 owns.
findings.requested_change: Correct the rationale references to the requirements that state each hold, ordering or refresh obligation.

findings.description: The revised SYS-TEST-012 text requires a 6–12 ms interval from the preceding cycle's refresh for every included cycle. Its rationale checks only cycle association for the first cycle after startup if no prior refresh exists. The same first-refresh trace has different criteria, and CON-SUP-106 defines the window relative to a previous refresh.
findings.requested_change: Align the requirement and test on when a previous refresh is needed. Make the first-refresh verdict depend explicitly on the approved policy in OP-SYS-010.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-008 requires execution-time measurement only through completion or limit expiry, whichever comes first. SYS-SUP-007 forbids an overrun for a completed execution with a measured value at or below the limit. If the release finishes after expiry, substituting its last required sample at expiry for a completion measurement can suppress the CON-SUP-103 overrun.
findings.requested_change: Make the no-overrun comparison apply to a defined completion measurement and state how expiry takes precedence when measurement ends before completion. Exercise a release that finishes after expiry.

findings.description: OP-SYS-009 estimates the earliest software reset request at about 1.3 ms after safe-state entry using the longest default entity width for its shortest report. Under CON-SUP-007 and CON-SUP-112, a 13-character line with T_IN and a one-digit timestamp takes about 1.13 ms. The estimate also needs to distinguish the CON-SUP-110 reset request from the reset event that actually cuts off transmission.
findings.requested_change: Recalculate the service time ranges using the actual allowed frame lengths. State the assumptions about reset-request latency and identify the physical reset event used for the interruption verdict.

findings.description: OP-SYS-043 proposes evidence methods for CON-SUP-110 retention. The target and Renode reset behavior, startup handling of retained state and validity of the latch, history and reset-sequence records after an interrupted update remain unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Establish the retention and startup behavior for each covered reset path and define the recovery outcome for each interrupted update. Tie the planned test or analysis to those outcomes.

findings.description: The revised rationale fails a slot at the end of the following task period if it never completes. The requirement text still uses only execution-limit expiry. Under a processor-time interpretation of CON-SUP-103, an indefinitely preempted release may never reach expiry, and another release can complete in time to satisfy the SYS-SUP-001 alive rule.
findings.requested_change: Identify the finite observation rule as an explicit verification criterion and justify its applicability to each scheduled release. Record any approval needed for the completion expectation it adds.

findings.description: SYS-TEST-015 proposes withholding T_IN completion only from alive supervision so timing and flow remain valid under SYS-SUP-003 and SYS-SUP-005. OP-SYS-038 leaves that stimulus unapproved. Without an admitted isolating stimulus under CON-SUP-116, SYS-TEST-006 still lacks its stated positive control.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved isolating stimulus and require evidence that alive supervision missed the completions while timing and flow remained valid through the end of the alive window.

findings.description: V2 cites suppressing T_IN releases as a possible way to isolate the alive cutoff. The revised SYS-SUP-005 makes each skipped scheduled release a missing checkpoint at its cycle end, so that stimulus produces an earlier flow fault. The SYS-WDG-003 rationale also omits the proposed alive-only stimulus now in SYS-TEST-015.
findings.requested_change: Remove release suppression as an isolating candidate and align V2 with the proposed or approved OP-SYS-038 stimulus. Require evidence that the alive rule alone makes the boundary refresh ineligible.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 specifies milliseconds since start. The item selects the latest reset and refers to when the controller started without identifying an observable reference event. OP-SYS-007 leaves the origin open.
findings.requested_change: Use the approved observable timestamp origin and define the expected timestamp at the startup boundary.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-001 excludes a period whose control cycle starts before the startup checks pass. CON-SUP-107 prevents release before the checks pass but permits a later release in that same cycle under the scheduling information supplied. CON-SUP-101 and CON-SUP-102 leave startup alignment and the first T_DIAG release phase open.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved first-period rule and T_DIAG phase, including the case where a cycle starts before startup checks pass and a release is scheduled after they pass.

findings.description: With truncation, a start 2.05 ms after release can measure 2.0 ms and satisfy the no-fault rule. CON-SUP-103 classifies starts later than the configured limit as late. OP-SYS-027 leaves the mapping near the limit open.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved mapping and specify verdicts for starts exactly at the limit and immediately on either side of it.

findings.description: The 11 s high-status interval starts at the SYS-TEST-004 status edge. CON-SUP-108 gives 11 s for a runtime integrity pass with a different origin. STK-SUP-015 and CON-SUP-116 establish simulator testability, and the demonstration duration remains an author proposal.
findings.requested_change: Use the approved demonstration duration and origin, then align the dependent nominal-run criteria.

findings.description: The 1099-cycle minimum assumes the first complete cycle starts within 10 ms of the status edge. CON-SUP-101 defines the cycle duration and CON-SUP-109 defines the status signal. Neither establishes the relationship needed for this count.
findings.requested_change: Base the cycle count on approved cycle alignment and observation duration, or use an approved progression criterion with an independent observation origin.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 leaves the endpoint of the 10 ms fault-report deadline open. The rationale measures through transmission of the line feed while OP-SYS-007 still records the choice between transmission start and completion.
findings.requested_change: State the approved observable transmission endpoint and apply it in each dependent test.

findings.description: The flow-fault entity is the affected task. One CON-SUP-104 evaluation can find several missing or out-of-order checkpoints, and CON-SUP-112 provides no selection rule for the task name in that case.
findings.requested_change: Specify which entity or entities the controller reports when one flow evaluation finds multiple bad checkpoints.

findings.description: When equally timed detections straddle the eight-report cutoff, either tied report can be displaced. CON-SUP-113 fixes the returned count and leaves that tie open.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved ordering for equal detection times and cover a tie across the eighth-report cutoff.

findings.description: The CON-SUP-110 latch rule still leaves the effect of an intervening watchdog or other reset undefined. The rationale describes operation after startup checks, while the requirement gives no precise event that starts the 60 s fault-free interval.
findings.requested_change: Define the reset events that break the sequence and the observable start and end events for the 60 s interval.

findings.description: CON-SUP-104 and CON-SUP-105 place flow evaluation at cycle end. The revised item handles a skipped release, but a checkpoint received exactly at cycle end still has no verdict until OP-SYS-036 determines receipt and evaluation precedence.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved precedence to coincident receipt and specify how verification establishes coincidence.

findings.description: A preempted task can use less processor time than its CON-SUP-103 limit while exceeding the same limit in elapsed time. The no-overrun decision depends on the execution-time measure still open in OP-SYS-013.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved execution-time measure and exercise a preempted release that separates the two possible verdicts.

findings.description: SYS-TEST-014 now requires a complete STS frame and its rationale times the end of that frame from the last request character. OP-SYS-007 leaves both CON-SUP-113 measurement events open. A frame beginning before the deadline and ending after it can produce different verdicts.
findings.requested_change: Use the same approved request and response timing events as SYS-DIAG-007 and state the demonstration's deadline against those events.

findings.description: SYS-DIAG-003 assigns code 8 to watchdog resets and SYS-DIAG-002 requires an entity for each report. The allowed task, CODE and CONFIG values in CON-SUP-112 give no watchdog-reset entity.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved entity for code 8 and cover it in the watchdog-reset report test.

findings.description: The GET FAULTS trigger applies whenever a request is received. A CON-SUP-110 reset can interrupt a pending response, and the set leaves acceptance and reply behavior in the retained safe state open.
findings.requested_change: Define request acceptance and response disposition before a pending reset, during recovery and while the safe state is latched.

findings.description: The first transmitted bit supplies the only history-entry deadline. If a watchdog reset prevents transmission from starting, that event never occurs. CON-SUP-110 requires retained history across watchdog reset, and OP-SYS-015 leaves the status of the detected fault open.
findings.requested_change: Specify the entry or recovery outcome when reset preempts the first bit, and verify the first GET FAULTS response after the restart.

findings.description: The less-than-100 ms refresh obligation applies whenever no listed task fault has become detectable since reset. This includes startup and retained-latch operation, where CON-SUP-106 leaves the independent-watchdog service policy open.
findings.requested_change: State the modes in which refresh is required and identify the reference event and bound for the first refresh in each applicable mode.

findings.description: The revised watchdog timeout criterion measures from the previous refresh. It gives no reference if the window watchdog is active and its first refresh never occurs, a case relevant to the fallback reset in STK-SUP-005.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved activation and first-refresh policy and specify the required reset outcome if the first refresh is absent.

findings.description: CON-SUP-115 requires rejection of an unknown task. CON-SUP-101 names the default tasks but leaves the full supported identifier set open. A test cannot independently determine the verdict for an identifier outside the defaults.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved supported identifier set and use it to establish known and unknown input cases.

findings.description: CON-SUP-113 supplies the STS template. Request framing, permitted state values and the meaning of fault count remain open, so a verifier cannot form a complete request and predict its response for a known state and fault history.
findings.requested_change: Use the approved request framing, state values and fault-count definition to specify complete request and expected-response examples.

findings.description: The 50 ms deadline in CON-SUP-113 gives no agreed measurement events for receipt and transmission. A reply that starts within 50 ms and finishes later has no unique verdict.
findings.requested_change: Identify the approved request-side and response-side events and use them for the timing test.

findings.description: The CON-SUP-113 GET FAULTS response lacks agreed wire order and completion framing. A verifier cannot distinguish a complete response with fewer than eight reports, including an empty history, from an incomplete transmission.
findings.requested_change: Define report order, response framing and complete encodings for empty, partial and full histories.

findings.description: CON-SUP-113 gives a 50 ms limit without agreed measurement events for receiving GET FAULTS and transmitting its multi-record reply. A reply can start within the limit and finish outside it.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved timing events for the request and its reply, including a reply with zero records.

findings.description: CON-SUP-113 requires ERR for other requests. The requirement gives neither an approved recognition boundary nor a finite observation limit for the response. A test cannot establish when a complete unknown request was received or when a missing ERR fails.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved recognition boundary and ERR response bound, and give verification cases for a complete unknown request and an incomplete request.

findings.description: STK-SUP-007 and CON-SUP-107 identify the image and when to check it. The integrity criterion and reference are still open, leaving the test without an independent accept-or-reject verdict for a given image.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved integrity criterion and independently reproducible valid and invalid image fixtures.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107 and SYS-MEM-002 provide the CRC-32 polynomial. Different initial values, reflection settings or final XOR values can yield different CRCs for the same covered bytes.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved CRC parameter set and supply a known-answer check for the defined configuration-block encoding.

findings.description: CON-SUP-114 requires measurement at the configured core clock. The requirement supplies neither the clock setting nor a controlled simulator configuration that identifies it, leaving the measurement conditions unreproducible.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved clock setting or the controlled simulator configuration that supplies it.

findings.description: The test sets reset flags and checks that classification follows the flags. CON-SUP-111 names five classes, and the expected classification for combined or retained flags remains open.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved mapping and flag precedence, and test the expected class for each relevant single, combined and retained flag pattern.

findings.description: CON-SUP-111 requires a startup message carrying the classified reset cause. Without approved framing and encoding, the verifier cannot identify the message or decode the cause.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved startup frame and the encoding of each reset class.

findings.description: The stated test must establish that both outputs are low from any reset under CON-SUP-109. CON-SUP-003 and CON-SUP-005 give no evidence that the simulator represents external output levels during reset assertion and before GPIO configuration.
findings.requested_change: Establish evidence for the external levels on each reset path and use a verification method that covers reset assertion, early startup and the software-controlled interval.

findings.description: CON-SUP-109 requires status low from any reset, including one taken while SYS-SAFE-006 has status high. The test lacks evidence of the external pin level during reset assertion and before software acts.
findings.requested_change: Verify the external level from reset assertion, including a reset from high status, using approved pin behavior and evidence for each reset path.

findings.description: The startup fault test checks that neither output is high at any recorded sample. A trace starting after software begins can miss the reset interval and early transitions that the continuous CON-SUP-109 hold covers.
findings.requested_change: Cover the preceding reset and early startup with approved pin-level evidence, and use transition evidence to verify the uninterrupted hold for each startup fault.

findings.description: The sampled status trace can show low at fault injection while missing a high level during the preceding reset or before the first sample. SYS-SAFE-008 and CON-SUP-109 require the uninterrupted interval from reset.
findings.requested_change: Combine approved reset-interval evidence with status-transition observation through the fault and subsequent reset.

findings.description: The startup demonstration checks for the SYS-RST-009 message. Because CON-SUP-111 leaves the frame identity open, its presence cannot be distinguished from an FLT line or other simulated startup output.
findings.requested_change: Identify the expected startup frame in the demonstration using the approved message format.

findings.description: The isolated CON-SUP-107 code-integrity demonstration requires a complete code 5 report. If the computation never finishes and no report or reset occurs, the fallback observation limit still depends on an undefined startup duration.
findings.requested_change: Give the demonstration a finite failure point from an observable startup event, including a run with no computation completion, report or reset.

findings.description: The isolated CON-SUP-107 configuration-integrity demonstration requires a complete code 6 report. A run whose CRC check never finishes and produces no report or reset still has no defined observation limit.
findings.requested_change: Use an approved startup observation bound that yields a failure verdict when the CRC computation never finishes.

findings.description: The CON-SUP-115 range-fault test ends relative to the fault's detectability or an undefined fallback startup limit. When the range check never runs, its detectability event never occurs and absence of code 9 has no finite failure point.
findings.requested_change: Set a finite observation limit from startup that applies even if the range check never runs.

findings.description: If a watchdog is active during the CON-SUP-107 startup checks, the time remaining after a failing computation can be too short for the CON-SUP-110 report and software reset sequence. The startup watchdog policy and timing evidence remain open.
findings.requested_change: Establish the remaining watchdog time for each startup failure path and state the required outcome if it cannot accommodate reporting and software reset.

findings.description: The startup ordering applies when the failed check leads to a software reset request. A watchdog active during startup can reset the controller after the failed computation and before the report starts. CON-SUP-106 and CON-SUP-107 provide no timing basis that excludes this path.
findings.requested_change: Define the approved report and reset outcome for a startup failure preempted by a watchdog, and verify that sequence.

findings.description: The continuous latched hold under CON-SUP-109 and CON-SUP-110 includes reset assertion and the interval before software acts. CON-SUP-003 gives no pin or board evidence that both outputs stay driven low during those intervals.
findings.requested_change: Establish the hardware mechanism and evidence that maintain both external levels through each reset in the latched state.

findings.description: The latched status hold spans every intervening reset. CON-SUP-003 gives no external status-pin behavior during reset or before GPIO setup. A simulator trace with no high sample cannot establish the continuous hold required by CON-SUP-109 and CON-SUP-110.
findings.requested_change: Establish the pin behavior and a verification method that covers assertion and early startup on each latched reset path.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-003 requires fault declaration at the exact CON-SUP-103 execution-limit expiry. Its rationale says exact declaration is infeasible and its test allows a tolerance awaiting approval. The 100 µs measurement resolution supplies no declaration tolerance.
findings.requested_change: Align the declaration bound and the verification tolerance with the approved latency from expiry.

findings.description: SYS-DIAG-002 requires a CON-SUP-112 report for every detected fault. Refresh cessation under SYS-WDG-007 can trigger the CON-SUP-106 reset before transmission starts or completes. The report outcome under that preemption remains open.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved reset precedence to the report deadline and define the outcome when transmission is cut off or never starts.

findings.description: SYS-DIAG-006 requires each detected fault to appear in history while fewer than eight faults have occurred. SYS-DIAG-010 permits entry by the first transmitted bit. A query or reset between detection and entry has different allowed histories under those rules and CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-113.
findings.requested_change: Define one approved point at which a report becomes part of the observable and reset-surviving history. Align the membership and entry requirements with it.

findings.description: From the eighth detection onward, SYS-DIAG-011 changes required history membership at detection. SYS-DIAG-010 permits later entry. A GET FAULTS query or reset in that interval leaves the new report and any displaced report unresolved under CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-113.
findings.requested_change: Define the approved transition for adding the new report and removing the displaced report, including the result of reading or resetting during the transition.

findings.description: A flow fault at the end of a nominal 10 ms cycle can suppress the refresh with about 2 ms remaining before the CON-SUP-106 window expires. A hardware reset can then preempt the CON-SUP-110 software reset request and keep the incident out of the supervisor-reset latch count.
findings.requested_change: State the approved reset precedence and the effect on latch counting when a watchdog expires during the fault reaction sequence.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 orders safe-state entry before report transmission. With refresh withheld under SYS-WDG-007, a CON-SUP-106 reset can preempt safe-state entry or transmission start. The requirement gives no outcome for that path.
findings.requested_change: Define the approved output and reporting outcomes across a watchdog reset that preempts safe-state entry or the start of transmission.

findings.description: CON-SUP-111 requires the service tool to read the latest reset cause. Neither CON-SUP-113 response includes it and other requests receive ERR. The approved interaction that satisfies both decisions remains open.
findings.requested_change: Identify the approved service-tool interaction and reconcile its framing and availability with CON-SUP-113.

findings.description: SYS-RST-013 requires transmission through the terminating line feed before the software reset request. A CON-SUP-106 watchdog reset can interrupt the report before the request, leaving the conditional ordering satisfied while the CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-112 report remains incomplete.
findings.requested_change: Define the required report completion or recovery behavior when a watchdog reset precedes the software reset request.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-003 declares overrun when execution is incomplete at expiry. SYS-SUP-007 forbids it for a completion measured at or below the limit. Under a mapping still allowed by OP-SYS-027, a completion shortly after expiry can satisfy both predicates.
findings.requested_change: Use one approved boundary rule for expiry, quantization and completion so the two requirements give the same verdict around the limit.

findings.description: The watchdog cutoff uses physical start-limit expiry for a late release. SYS-SUP-002 classifies lateness when the measured delay first exceeds the limit. If a refresh falls between those events, its eligibility can depend on whether the task subsequently starts before the measured crossing.
findings.requested_change: Use a cutoff the controller can determine at refresh time, aligned with the approved timing comparison. Test the interval between physical expiry and the measured crossing if one remains.

findings.description: SYS-WDG-005 now governs the independent watchdog only. A task fault can become detectable near that watchdog's 100 ms expiry under SYS-WDG-001 and CON-SUP-106. Withholding refresh can then cause a hardware reset ahead of the CON-SUP-110 report and software reset.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved reset precedence to independent-watchdog expiry and cover a fault detected near that expiry.

findings.description: The inclusive refresh prohibition can cause a CON-SUP-106 window-watchdog reset before the CON-SUP-110 report and software reset request. That reset can interrupt the report and is classified separately from the same-code supervisor resets that drive the latch.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved precedence to refresh cessation, report completion, reset-cause classification and same-code latch counting.
